habitat: Hill dipterocarp forest; primary/secondary montane forest; and forest edge at 930–3000 m
story: In the diverse world of birds, the Whitehead Trogon (Arachnothera juliae) stands out. This species, part of the Nectariniidae family, is a resident of Hill dipterocarp forest; primary/secondary montane forest; and forest edge at 930–3000 m. Its IUCN Red List status is Least Concern (LC), which serves as a call to action for habitat preservation. The Whitehead Trogon is more than just a bird; it is a symbol of the rich biodiversity that we must protect. Through this poster, we hope to foster a greater understanding and appreciation for the Whitehead Trogon and its role in the ecosystem.
Every poster is crafted to inspire curiosity about our planet's incredible biodiversity.
